handoff: Fix addresses the cause and the repro test passes (typecheck and 1205 tests green). Blocking F1: the check order stores the whole process env (tokens included) in ~/.norn/checks/<run_id>.json (0644), although check-run already inherits it, and orders left by a dead check-run are never removed. Minor: status shows the step's age rather than the check's (F2); a check-run that fails before writing its receipt reruns silently (F3); nits F4/F5.

findings.title: The check order writes the whole process env (secrets included) to disk
findings.detail:
`env = definedOnly({ ...process.env, ...act.ctx.env, ...readEnvNorn(a.cwd), ...a.env, NORN_HOME })` goes into the order, which is written to ~/.norn/checks/<run_id>.json via atomicWriteJson (mode 0644, fsx.ts:35). In `norn watch` that env holds whatever the person's shell has: GH_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, cloud credentials. Nothing needs it on disk: the detached `norn check-run` is spawned with `env: { ...process.env, ...act.ctx.env }` (line 74) and so already inherits those. The file is removed only by runCheckOrder's finally; a check-run killed before then (crash, reboot, kill -9) leaves it forever, because the rerun gets a new run_id from decide (`ctx.id()`, steps.ts) and nothing sweeps ~/.norn/checks. The implementer flagged this in handoff ('stores the check's full env (incl. process env)'). Repro: run a check step and `cat ~/.norn/checks/*.json` while it runs; every exported variable is there.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Store only what the tick adds: `.env.norn`, the action's env and NORN_HOME (or read .env.norn in check-run), and merge it over the inherited process.env in runCheckOrder. Write the order with mode 0600. Remove orphaned orders when a dead check lease is reclaimed (or sweep orders whose lease is gone). Add a test asserting that a variable only in process.env is absent from the order.

findings.title: `norn status` does not show the check as running with the check's age
findings.detail:
Wanted: '`norn status` shows the check as running with its age.' Only the inbox item changed (items.ts: '(check running)' since lease.created_at). `norn status` prints `running test#1 <age>` from stateText, using the step's age (step_entered_at), the same text as before the change and the same for a queued check; its Runs section lists only `state.run`, which run_check does not set. The inbox does meet the intent, so this is minor, but the status line cannot tell a running check from a queued one.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Either mark a leased check in the status line (e.g. `running test#1 (check running 2m)`) or list check leases under Runs, with a formatStatus test.

findings.title: A check-run that fails before its receipt reruns on every tick and leaves no trace
findings.detail:
The child is spawned with `stdio: "ignore"`, so nothing it prints is kept. When `norn check-run` exits without a receipt (an unreadable order → refuse; an exception in stopStrayListeners/writeLog/appendReceipt), its lease is released (finally) or left dead and reclaimed (K3), and decide emits run_check again on the next tick. That repeats forever with no receipt, no act_failure and no counter. Before this change the same exception was thrown inside act and showed up as an act failure on the story. Unlikely (the order is validated before it is written), but it fails silently when it does happen.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Send check-run's stderr to the run's log file, or have runCheckOrder write a `fail` receipt (with the error as output) from a catch, so a broken check-run ends the step instead of looping.

findings.title: Lease handoff can recreate a lease the check-run already released
findings.detail:
`if (holder && readText(file) !== null) updateLease(...)` is check-then-act: if check-run releases the lease between the readText and updateLease (a very short command), updateLease (atomicWriteJson) writes it back with the now-dead check-run as holder. K3 reclaims it on the next tick, and the receipt already exists, so the impact is one tick of `check.running`. Similarly, when `identify` returns null the lease keeps the tick's holder, which under `norn watch` is the long-lived watch process: a check-run that dies then leaves a lease that is never reclaimed until watch exits.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Use a compare-and-swap (store already has removeIfUnchanged; a replaceIfUnchanged would do), and treat a null identify as an error that releases the lease.

findings.title: Double blank line before definedOnly
findings.detail:
Two empty lines between runCheckOrder and definedOnly; elsewhere in the file functions are separated by one.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Remove one.
